topic: Infinite Feedback: Holomorphic Dynamics and Iterated Functions
target_audience: University students in STEM or advanced mathematics enthusiasts

sections.title: The Complex Playground (Prerequisites)
lecture_lines: The complex plane provides our mathematical stage.
Point z represents a coordinate in this space.
A vector defines the position from the origin.
Holomorphic functions transform the plane's geometry.
Local angles remain preserved throughout the transformation.
animations: Create a 2D coordinate grid in #555555 for the complex plane.
Fade in point 'z' at (2, 1) with label 'z = x + iy' in #FFFFFF.
Draw a #00FFFF vector from the origin to point 'z'.
Transform the entire grid using f(z) = z^2 while preserving 90-degree intersections.
Zoom in on a grid intersection to highlight angle preservation in #FFFF00.

sections.title: The Feedback Loop: Iteration
lecture_lines: Iteration feeds a function's output back as its next input.
The sequence of positions creates a path called an orbit.
These orbits reveal the long-term behavior of the system.
animations: Display the iteration formula z_{n+1} = f(z_n) in #FFFFFF at top-center.
Animate a point z_0 moving to z_1 via a #FF00FF curved arrow.
Continue the path through z_2 and z_3, leaving a #00FF00 trail.

sections.title: Escape or Stay: The Fate of Orbits
lecture_lines: The quadratic map shifts points through feedback.
Stable orbits spiral toward a fixed destination.
Unstable orbits accelerate away toward infinity.
animations: Show the quadratic map formula f(z) = z^2 + c in #FFFFFF.
Display a point spiraling into the origin in #00FF00 (stable orbit).
Display a point flying off the screen in #FF0000 (unstable orbit).

sections.title: The Julia Set: The Edge of Chaos
lecture_lines: This boundary is the Julia set, a complex fractal.
It is the thin, chaotic edge between staying and escaping.
Zooming in reveals self-similar patterns repeating at every scale.
Small changes here lead to radically different future outcomes.
The Julia set's structure depends entirely on the constant c.
animations: Draw the Julia set boundary for c = -0.8 + 0.156i in #FF8C00.
Perform a deep zoom into a branch of the Julia set.
Flash a sub-region and scale it to show self-similarity in #FFFFFF.
Animate two nearly identical points on the boundary diverging rapidly.
Smoothly morph the set's shape by varying 'c' to #00BFFF.

sections.title: The Mandelbrot Set: The Master Map
lecture_lines: The Mandelbrot set maps every possible value of c.
It acts as a master catalog for all Julia sets.
Points inside the set produce connected, intricate Julia shapes.
Outside points create disconnected clouds of mathematical dust.
It represents the bridge between order and chaotic feedback.
animations: Display the complex parameter plane with 'c' axes in #888888.
Fill the Mandelbrot set region where orbits stay bounded in #AA00FF.
Highlight an interior 'c' point and its connected Julia set thumbnail.
Highlight an exterior 'c' point and its disconnected dust Julia set.
Zoom into the Mandelbrot boundary to reveal infinite, repeating detail.

sections.title: Natural Feedback and Applications
lecture_lines: These dynamics mirror feedback loops found throughout our world.
From Romanesco broccoli to fractal antennas, nature iterates.
Infinite complexity emerges from these simple, repeating rules.
